title: Regret Topology: sampling-based quantization sensitivity probe
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a working note for an experimental method I’m calling a "regret topology" probe. Goal: map how different quantization modes (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) and kernel choices produce a joint surface of quality degradation (regret) vs. latency/cost across representative request types and client mixes. The topology approach emphasizes sampling across two axes simultaneously: workload semantics (short prompts, long contexts, streaming tokens) and model internal sensitivity (per-layer perturbation samples).

Why do this now?
- We keep getting edge cases where a quant config looks fine on avg but creates pockets of high regret matched with bad tail latency (e.g., long-context summarization on AWQ kernels).
- Existing one-dimensional sweeps (QLoss vs latency or per-layer sensitivity lists) don’t reveal whether particular request subclasses and kernel choices interact adversarially.
- We want a practical artifact the product team can use: a map that flags configurations with unacceptable pockets of user-visible regressions even when global metrics pass.

High-level idea (methodology):
1) Select a diverse sample of requests from production traces and synthetic probes. Group into workload buckets: chat-turns (interactive, short), summarization (medium-long), code-completion (long, repetitive tokens), and embeddings-like short-stable queries.
2) For each request, create multiple perturbed inference runs: different quant modes + kernel combo + small per-layer weight/noise perturbations (simulate sensitivity to quantization rounding). The per-layer perturbation is small and deterministic (seeded) to reveal brittle layers.
3) For each run, measure latency profile (p50/p95/p99, cold start, token-throughput), cost-per-token (model-inference-cycle accounting), and quality metrics: token-perplexity delta, and downstream task metric where applicable (e.g., F1/EM on a QA probe, Rouge for summarization). From these compute a regret score per request-run (normalized composite).
4) Aggregate into a 2D topology: X axis = workload sample index ordered by a semantic embedding distance (clusters placed so similar requests are adjacent). Y axis = quant-kernel variants. Color = regret; height/contour = p95 latency delta (or cost). This surface highlights pockets where quant choice+kernel is bad for a subset of requests.

Experimental setup (provisioned harness):
- Hardware: A100 80GB (prod-like), H100 80GB, and a T4 as a low-power comparison. All tests run on dedicated capacity to remove noisy neighbors; we still record micro-variance by repeating runs.
- Runtime build: rw-runtime@bench-regret-topology-202808. Uses the latest kernel switcher with AWQ and GPTQ kernels compiled from kernel-tuner-0.9.
- Models: open-llama-13b-ggml (as synthetic), and two prod variants (redwood-verified-13b-v2, redwood-verified-70b-v1) — we only run the 70b for short-sample probes due to cost.
- Quant modes: int8 per-channel symmetric, fp8 (E4M3-like), GPTQ (8-bit per-group), AWQ (as released), and a mixed fallback profile (int8 primary + fp8 fallback for attention layers).
- Kernels: native-cuda-matmuls, tensor-core-optimized, awq-vecpack, gptq-block-optim. We pair each quant mode with best-known kernel and then also with a mismatched kernel to see failure modes.
- Workload samples: 2.5k unique requests sampled from last 30 days of prod logs (privacy filtered), plus 500 synthetics crafted to stress attention length and repetitive tokens. Workloads are bucketed and labeled.

Metrics and regret definition: (note: trying to keep this simple but actionable)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end (client -> first-byte -> stream end), token-emission interval distribution.
- Cost: approximated as GPU-seconds per token (normalized to base run on fp32).
- Quality metrics: 
  * Per-token logprob delta averaged across sequence (normalized)
  * Task-specific metrics: QA EM/F1, Rouge-L for summarization, pass@1 for code completion where applicable.
- Regret score: composite 0..1: 0 = no measurable drop vs baseline (fp32 baseline), 1 = severe drop. Construction: weighted sum (0.6 * normalized quality delta + 0.3 * quality-task-failure-flag + 0.1 * semantic-variance). Today weights are subjective — need to iterate.

Preliminary findings (high-level):
- AWQ + awq-vecpack kernel shows excellent cost-reduction for chat-turns (short), with flat latency improvements (p50 reduced ~28%) and low average regret. However, for long-context summarization bucket we observed a cluster (~3% of samples) with high regret (regret>0.6) correlated with a single attention block in layer 21 — signals that AWQ rounding there flips a high-leverage attention head.
- GPTQ on tensor-core-optimized kernels gives stable average quality for medium workloads but exhibits higher p99 latency variance on H100 when memory packing falls back (observed 12% tail increase). This was not visible on A100 because of different kernel memory layout.
- FP8 gives moderate cost gains and smooth quality tradeoffs, but combined with native-cuda-matmuls kernel it sometimes increases token emission jitter for streaming workloads; p95 latency jitter increases by ~15ms for small tokens, which users perceive as stuttering.
- Mixed-fallback profile (int8 primary, fp8 attention fallback) eliminated most AWQ long-context regressions at cost ~8% extra GPU time vs pure AWQ, with p95 tail unaffected. This looks promising as a practical safety fallback.

Notable failure modes and brittle signatures we observed: 
- Single-layer flip: small perturbation in a mid-layer attention projection leads to large upstream decoding drift (cascading). These occur rarely but map to pockets in the topology surface — the main utility of the visualization.
- Kernel mismatch: Running GPTQ quant tables on an awq-vecpack kernel produced deterministic token-synthesis artifacts (rare but reproducible). Recommendation: runtime should validate kernel-quant compatibility at startup with a small set of golden-decoding tests.
- Memory packing fallback path: when packing fails and runtime switches to a slower matmul path, p99 spikes. This is combative when quant reduces precision and kernel code paths assume blocked memory layouts.

Practical recommendations (for product/ops):
1) Add an automated "regret pocket" check to nightly builds: run a small sample (200 requests across buckets) across quant profiles; if any pocket with regret>0.5 and p95 latency delta > 25% exists, fail the candidate.
2) Ship mixed-fallback profiles as default for Dedicated customers with long-context workloads (config flag enable_mixed_quant_fallback=true).
3) Kernel-quant compatibility matrix: make it explicit in model catalog and gate deployment when incompatible pairs are requested.
4) Add a microtest harness in CI that runs a kernel sanity decode (golden seeds) to catch deterministic artifacts before prod push.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self and team):
- Need to formalize weights for the regret composite metric. Talk to product/UX to understand user-visible thresholds (what regret level correlates with tickets?).
- Re-run the same probe on smaller GPU types (T4) with simulated load to understand cost tradeoffs for edge deployments.
- More rigorous statistical analysis of per-layer sensitivity: can we build a small classifier that predicts brittle layers and upweight them for fp8 fallback?
- Visual design: the 2D topology is useful but we should prototype a drill-down UI in Console where you can click a high-regret cell and view the exact request, kernel trace, and per-layer gradients.

Appendix: short reproducibility checklist (for the next engineer)
- Branch: rw-runtime@bench-regret-topology-202808
- Node config: dedicated A100 x1 (no multi-tenant), GPU clock settings unchanged, CUDA driver 12.3, cuBLAS tuned off (so kernel differences are clear).
- Seed list: seeds/regen-202808-200.lst (on s3 bucket, internal).
- Commands: scripts/bench/regret_topology/run_probe.sh --model redwood-verified-13b-v2 --quant awq,gptq,fp8,int8 --kernels awq-vecpack,tensorcore,native --repeats 8 --output-dir /tmp/regret-probe-aug2028
- Expected runtime: ~6h per model on single A100 for the 3k request sweep (including repeats).

Notes to self: capture snapshots of the topology surface (svg + csv) and upload to confluence page. Ping SRE about adding a small runtime health check for kernel compatibility. Schedule a 30-min sync with Product (Linh) to align on regret thresholds.
